narrative: In March 2022 a big storm hit our house and wind-driven rain got in through the lead flashing around our Dutch gable roof. It's cracked the ceiling and cornices in the master bedroom, cracked a wall, and now there's mould starting from the water getting in. The insurer's assessor tried to say it was wear and tear but our own roofer says it was the storm.

gold_extraction.cause: wind-driven rain entered through Dutch gable lead flashing during storm
gold_extraction.damaged_item: master bedroom ceiling, cornices, wall, with resulting mould

notes: Article gives no repair dollar estimate, only $5,000 report-cost + $1,000 stress compensation awarded by AFCA -- those are AFCA remedies, not the claimant's original estimated_amount, so left null. Exact storm date not given beyond 'March 2022' -- used the 1st as a placeholder, please correct if you find/prefer a different convention for day-unknown dates.

narrative: A hailstorm on 31 October 2020 dropped hailstones the size of golf balls and punched holes straight through our old asbestos corrugated roof, and it damaged the patio roof next to it too. The insurer said it was mostly decayed material that just needed replacing anyway, but the hail definitely did the damage.

narrative: A flexihose under our kitchen sink burst in March 2022 and flooded the kitchen. It damaged the sink cabinet and kickboards. Our tenant's plumber replaced the hose before anyone photographed it, and by the time the insurer's assessor came out in October we'd already had the kitchen renovated. We claimed $15,400 total for the kitchen.
notes: AFCA only ultimately allowed the sink-cabinet/kickboard portion of the $15,400 claim (rejected the rest as unlikely to have been affected) -- gold_extraction here reflects what was CLAIMED, not what was AWARDED; decide which one this project's schema is meant to capture (claimed vs. awarded amount) and apply that consistently across all AFCA-sourced rows, since real disputes almost always have both numbers.

narrative: During a huge storm in February 2022 we got over 700mm of rain in five days and our house, which sits a bit below street level, flooded through the western wall foundations. Multiple rooms were affected. The insurer tried to knock it back under a 'seepage' exclusion but it wasn't gradual seepage, it was the storm.

gold_extraction.cause: extreme rainfall overwhelmed western wall foundations, water entered via overflow

notes: Same storm-vs-flood classification question as row 3 -- AFCA's own finding was 'storm event' as dominant cause (not flood), so labeled storm here, but worth a consistent team decision on the enum boundary since several real cases sit right on this line. No dollar figure in source -- null.
